1.s: “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity,” says the Preacher. Generations come and go, the sun rises and sets, and there is nothing new under the sun.
1.d: The Teacher, Qoheleth in Hebrew, is called David’s son, which likely points to Solomon [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 1:1]]. “Vanity” translates hebel, which means “breath” or “vapour” [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 1:2]].

2.s: The Teacher tries pleasure, great building projects, wealth and wisdom, and finds it all vapour, since everyone dies. Yet eating and enjoying work is a gift from God.
2.d: Seeking pleasure for its own sake is empty, and even great achievements are like smoke [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 2:1–11]]. Yet enjoying one’s work “is from the hand of God” [[bible:Ecclesiastes 2:24]].

3.s: “For everything there is a season”: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to weep and a time to laugh. God has set eternity in human hearts.
3.d: Wisdom knows that everything has its own time [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 3:1–8]]. God has planted eternity in each of us, enough to be in awe of him and to hope for life after death [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 3:11]].

4.s: Oppression, envy and loneliness. “Two are better than one… a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”
4.d: Oppression is everywhere [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 4:1]], and most people are driven by competition, so the Teacher urges moderation instead of envy [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 4:4]]. “A threefold cord is not quickly broken” [[bible:Ecclesiastes 4:12]].

5.s: Guard your steps in God’s house; let your words be few; keep your vows. Wealth does not satisfy, and you leave with nothing.
5.d: God’s house is mainly a place for listening [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 5:1]]. “Pay that which you vow” is almost a quotation of the law in Deuteronomy 23 [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 5:4–5]].

6.s: A man may have riches and a hundred children and still not enjoy them.
6.d: It is a sad tragedy when someone succeeds but cannot enjoy it [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 6:1–2]]; people often feel unsatisfied whatever they have [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 6:7]].

7.s: Better the house of mourning than the house of feasting. Don’t be overly righteous or overly wise. “There is not a righteous man on earth who does good and doesn’t sin.”
7.d: These sayings are like those in the book of Proverbs [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 7:1–4]]. Thinking soberly about death teaches us to enjoy life wisely [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 7:3–4]], and no one is without sin [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 7:20]] [[bible:Romans 3:23]].

8.s: Obey the king. Wickedness is not always punished quickly, yet it will be well with those who fear God.
8.d: It is pointless to plot against the king’s power [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 8:3–4]]. Yet “it will be better with those who fear God” [[bible:Ecclesiastes 8:12]].

9.s: The same fate comes to all. So eat your bread with joy, love your spouse, and work with all your might. Time and chance happen to everyone.
9.d: There is no promise that doing good will bring rewards in this life [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 9:1]]. “Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might” [[bible:Ecclesiastes 9:10]].

10.s: A little folly outweighs wisdom; proverbs about rulers, fools and work.
10.d: Giving power to those who cannot use it wisely is a great mistake [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 10:5–7]]. A blunt axe needs more strength, “but skill brings success” [[bible:Ecclesiastes 10:10]].

11.s: “Cast your bread on the waters.” Be generous and work, since you do not know what will prosper. Rejoice in youth, knowing God will judge.
11.d: All profitable work involves risk, so act wisely and trust God with the outcome [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 11:1–6]]; invest instead of hoarding [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 11:1–2]].

12.s: “Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth,” before old age, pictured as a house falling into ruin. The end of the matter: “Fear God, and keep his commandments.”
12.d: Remembering your Creator gives wisdom for life and for God’s judgement [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 12:1–2]]. The body is like a fragile clay jar [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 12:6]]. The closing note by an editor gives the conclusion: fear God and keep his commandments [[tosn:Ecclesiastes 12:9–14]] [[bible:Ecclesiastes 12:13]].
